Author: Vivek Rusia Bench: Vivek Rusia  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  CRA No. 10757 of 2023  (MANISH Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH )
 Dated : 08-11-2024

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Manish Yadav, counsel for the appellant.
Shri Gaurav Panchal, counsel for the objector.

Shri K.K.Tiwari, Government Advocate for the respondent/S Heard on I.A.No. 10608/2024 which is the second application filed under Section 389(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

The previous application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 11.10.2023.
02.

Appellant has been convicted vide judgment dated 21.07.2023. passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO), District Ratlam for offence punishable under Sections 376(3) and 366 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years and 10 years, respectively and Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years with fine and default stipulations.
03.

As per the case of the prosecution, father of the prosecutrix lodged a missing person report of his daughter, thereafter she was recovered by the police and case was registered against the appellant.
04.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
Prosecutrix had gone along with the appellant on her own will.
After being recovered, she was medically examined and no definite opinion was given about commission of offence.
Further, there is no DNA in the case.
Appellant has been convicted only because the prosecutrix was found to be below 16 years of age.
However, father of the prosecutrix has 2 CRA-10757-2023 admitted the age of the prosecutrix as 22 years.
Appellant has no criminal antecedent and he was 21 years of age at the time of commission of offence.
Appeal is of the year 2023 and its final disposal will take considerable time.
Hence, in such circumstances, prayer is made for suspension of the jail sentence and grant of bail.
05. Learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the application and prays for its rejection.

06. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the medical evidence, this Court is of the considered opinion that the application for suspension of custodial sentence moved on behalf of the present appellant deserves to be Manish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189304249/
1 allowed.
07.

entities.text: Manish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, I.A.No.10608/2024 is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond by the appellant - Manish in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousands Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court the execution of custodial part of the jail sentence shall remain suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.
The appellant after being released on bail, shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 21.01.2025 and on all such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court.
I.A.Nos.14238/2023 and 14239/2023 also stands disposed of.
List for final hearing in due course.
